artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan closing the consumer deploy propagation gap by moving the existing per-extension freshness check to per-dispatch granularity and injecting the signal into the dispatch brief.

memory_candidates.content: When an existing detector fails to prevent the defect it detects, check placement and granularity before concluding the detector is missing. In the agent-system deploy-freshness case, a pull-side staleness check already existed and already fired non-blockingly, but only once per top-level command and only onto the orchestrating session's stderr -- never into the context of the spawned subagent that actually read the stale file. The fix was to re-fire the same unchanged comparison at per-dispatch granularity (skill_preflight_update) and inject the result into the dispatch brief the agent reads, not to build a new detection mechanism. Generalizable rule: a signal's value is determined by whether it lands in the context that acts on it, at a moment when it can still change behavior. Cost note: a pull-side check (each repo checks only itself, only when used) scales with the checking repo's own size, while a push-side fleet scan scales with the consumer count -- the two differ by orders of magnitude and should never be traded off as if equivalent.
